title: Phil Brady's Bar & Grill
venue_description:
Phil Brady's Bar & Grill

Phil Brady's Bar & Grill is a mid-city Baton Rouge institution housed in a building dating to the 1940s, when it operated as Michael's Bar. The current nightclub has been open since 1978 under longtime owner Joe Hall, and it still carries the original bar, railing and mirrors from its earlier life. It is best known across Louisiana as the home of one of the longest continuously running blues jams in the country.

Atmosphere and Setting

Phil Brady's is a no-frills neighborhood bar with a stage tucked into one corner, pool tables, and a crowd that ranges from longtime regulars to touring musicians passing through Baton Rouge. The room has an unpretentious, lived-in feel that has made it a comfortable home base for the city's blues community for decades.

The Thursday Night Blues Jam

Founded in 1986 by Shannon “Bayou” Williford, the weekly Thursday blues jam has run virtually every week since, celebrating its 40th anniversary in 2025. The jam has served as a training ground for generations of Baton Rouge blues musicians, some of whom went on to national careers, and it continues to draw surprise sit-ins from touring artists passing through town. As one regular put it, at Brady's “you never know who you're gonna see.”

Other Programming

Beyond the Thursday jam, Phil Brady's regularly books local blues, rock and roots acts throughout the week and is a frequent stop on the Baton Rouge Blues Festival's satellite events calendar.

For Performers

The jam is a true walk-up, sit-in format built around a rotating house band, welcoming musicians of every experience level who want to play the blues alongside seasoned players.

Good to Know

Phil Brady's Bar & Grill is located at 4848 Government Street, Baton Rouge, LA 70806. Street parking is available around the building.

title: Le Chien Brewing Company
venue_description:
Le Chien Brewing Company

Le Chien Brewing Company is a dog-friendly craft brewery in downtown Denham Springs, a Livingston Parish city just east of Baton Rouge that anchors the eastern edge of the metro area's live music and craft beer scene. The taproom pours a rotating lineup of house-brewed beers alongside a food menu of pub favorites including wings, and it has become a regular gathering spot for local musicians and songwriters.

Atmosphere and Setting

The brewery has a relaxed, family- and pet-friendly taproom vibe, with indoor and patio seating in the heart of Denham Springs' small but growing downtown entertainment district.

Songwriter Open Mic

On the first and third Wednesday of each month, Le Chien hosts a Songwriter Open Mic led by local host Victoria Lea, inviting acoustic performers and songwriters from around the Baton Rouge area to share original material and covers in a welcoming, low-key setting over craft beer.

Other Programming

Le Chien also partners with local businesses on community events such as book-and-brew nights, and regularly features other live acoustic performers on non-open-mic nights.

For Performers

The open mic leans toward solo and acoustic singer-songwriter performances, making it a good fit for original material as well as covers.

Good to Know

Le Chien Brewing Company is located at 101 S. Hummel St., Denham Springs, LA 70726, about 20 minutes east of downtown Baton Rouge.

title: West Baton Rouge Museum
venue_description:
West Baton Rouge Museum

The West Baton Rouge Museum, nicknamed the “Sugarcane Museum,” sits on a historic parish complex in Port Allen just across the Mississippi River from downtown Baton Rouge. Alongside exhibits on the region's sugar industry and a collection of preserved plantation-era buildings, the museum has become a well-loved home for grassroots acoustic music traditions in the greater Baton Rouge area.

Atmosphere and Setting

Jams take place in an air-conditioned museum meeting room, with sessions occasionally moving to a historic Juke Joint on the museum grounds during cooler months. The setting is casual, family-friendly and rooted in the region's cultural history.

Old Time Music Open Jam

On the second Sunday of every month, guitarist Kent Louque leads an Old Time Music Open Jam built around early to mid-20th-century country songs. Attendance has ranged from a handful of pickers to more than thirty musicians strumming guitars, fiddles, mandolins and string bass, with new players of any skill level encouraged to join in.

Cajun Music Jam

The following week, on the third Sunday of the month, the Cajun French Music Association hosts a companion Cajun Jam at the museum, keeping South Louisiana's Cajun French musical tradition alive with fiddle, accordion and guitar players of all levels welcome to sit in.

Other Programming

The museum's broader calendar includes historical exhibits, a working 1904 World's Fair sugar mill model display, blacksmith demonstrations, and seasonal community events throughout the year.

For Performers

Both monthly jams are informal, drop-in sessions with no sign-up required — musicians are simply invited to bring an instrument and join the circle.

Good to Know

The West Baton Rouge Museum is located at 845 North Jefferson Avenue, Port Allen, LA 70767, just a few minutes from downtown Baton Rouge across the Horace Wilkinson Bridge.

title: Red Stick Social
venue_description:
Red Stick Social

Red Stick Social is a large, multi-purpose entertainment venue in Baton Rouge's Mid City area, combining a restaurant, full bar, bowling lanes and a stage under one roof. Since opening in 2019, it has positioned itself as one of the capital city's premier gathering spots for food, drinks and live entertainment.

Atmosphere and Setting

The space is spacious and modern, with a dedicated performance area, professional sound and lighting, and enough room to host everything from intimate acoustic nights to full-band showcases alongside its bowling and dining areas.

Open Jam Night

Red Stick Social hosts a weekly Thursday night Open Jam, welcoming solo performers, full bands and everyone in between to sign up for stage time. The house provides a five-piece acoustic drum kit, multiple microphones, keyboard and guitar amp plugins, and even camera stands so performers can record their sets, with a rotation of regular jam night hosts keeping the evening moving.

Other Programming

Beyond the weekly jam, Red Stick Social's calendar includes happy hours, themed dance nights, karaoke, watch parties for LSU and Saints games, and a weekend brunch series.

For Performers

Performers are asked to sign up in advance by emailing the venue's music team, after which they are placed on the evening's stage-time rotation.

Good to Know

Red Stick Social is located at 1503 Government St, Baton Rouge, LA 70802, in the heart of Mid City.
